title: Citation-Level Unfaithfulness of Small Language Models on Vietnamese Banking Regulation: A Provenance-Guarded RAG Benchmark
description:
RegRAG-VN: a QA-driven benchmark and provenance-guarded evaluation framework for Vietnamese banking and payment regulation, accompanying the IEEE-RIVF 2026 paper of the same title.

The benchmark holds 88 questions (64 answerable over State Bank of Vietnam circulars, decrees and laws, each with a verbatim gold passage and article-level Điều gold; 24 unanswerable probes whose gold label is an explicit abstention sentinel) and a two-tier corpus whose coverage invariant requires every retained question's gold passage to string-match an ingested instrument. The release contains the ingestion and evaluation code (including the provenance guard and the deterministic lexical scorer), the two-tier corpus, the raw ingested sources (redistributed as downloaded from official government sources; they remain under their original terms), the full 792-row generation-campaign log (3 models x 3 retrieval modes x 88 questions, single RTX 3090, 4-bit quantisation, greedy decoding), the retrieval-recall logs for both the sparse (BM25 + pyvi) and dense (BGE-M3) arms, the computed table inputs, and the paper PDF.

Every generation and evaluation record carries its corpus tier, retriever backend and quantisation tag; the aggregation guard refuses rows with unset or degraded provenance. The generation campaign ran on the Tier-1 development fixture and is disclosed as such in the paper; retrieval quality is measured on the full Tier-2 corpus.
